name: Blink Rate Analysis
description: Analyzes eye blink patterns for naturalness — AI often generates unnatural blink rates
algorithm: Blink Rate Analysis — Sensor/Physical Model Analyzer
mechanism:
This method analyzes eye blinking patterns for deepfake detection following Li et al. (2018) "In Ictu Oculi":

1. **Eye State Classification**: For each frame, the eye aspect ratio (EAR) is computed from eye landmarks: EAR = (‖p2−p6‖ + ‖p3−p5‖) / (2‖p1−p4‖), where p1-p6 are the eye contour landmarks. EAR drops significantly during blinks, enabling frame-level open/closed classification.

2. **Blink Event Detection**: Consecutive frames with low EAR form blink events. Each blink is characterized by duration (typically 100-400ms in natural blinking), amplitude (EAR change magnitude), and velocity profile (rapid closing, slightly slower opening following Evinger et al., 1991).

3. **Blink Rate Statistical Analysis**: The inter-blink interval (IBI) distribution is analyzed. Natural spontaneous blinking occurs at 15-20 blinks/minute with a characteristic IBI distribution following a gamma or log-normal model. Early deepfake methods produced subjects that rarely or never blinked — a key detection cue identified by Li et al. (2018).

4. **Blink Naturalness Assessment**: Individual blink kinematics are evaluated: natural blinks are bilateral (both eyes close simultaneously), show stereotyped velocity profiles, and exhibit physiological reflexes (increased blink rate during speech, periodic patterns). AI-generated blinks may appear unilateral, show unnatural velocity profiles, or lack expected behavioral correlations.

5. **Temporal Pattern Scoring**: The overall blink pattern is scored against natural human behavior models. Anomalies include: absence of blinks, unnatural blink rates, irregular blink dynamics, asymmetric blinking, or blinks that don't correspond to expected cognitive/behavioral triggers. The score quantifies deviation from natural blink physiology.
parameters:
Analysis type: sensor
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through blink rate analysis analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Li, Y. et al. (2018). In Ictu Oculi: Exposing AI Created Fake Videos by Detecting Eye Blinking. WIFS.
Rossler, A. et al. (2019). FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images. ICCV.
